walletHowItWorks.title: How Your Wallet Works
walletHowItWorks.eoaDetail: Your private key — secured by Privy MPC. Never stored in one place.
walletHowItWorks.scaDetail: Your on-chain wallet. Holds USDC, pays gas via Paymaster, supports batched txns.
walletHowItWorks.sectionEoaBody: Your Externally Owned Account (EOA) is a standard Ethereum wallet backed by a private key. Kura secures it through Privy's MPC (Multi-Party Computation) — the key is cryptographically split across multiple secure enclaves, so no single server ever holds the full key. It acts purely as a signer.
walletHowItWorks.sectionScaTitle: SCA — The Wallet You Spend From
walletHowItWorks.sectionScaBody: Your Smart Contract Account (SCA) is a Safe smart wallet deployed on Base. It is the address your funds actually live in. Because it's a smart contract, it supports ERC-4337 account abstraction — meaning gas fees can be sponsored (Paymaster), multiple actions can be batched into one transaction, and social recovery can be added in the future.
walletHowItWorks.sectionWhyBody: Separating the signer (EOA) from the spending wallet (SCA) gives you the best of both worlds: the flexibility of smart accounts with the simplicity of a passkey-secured key. If you ever need to migrate to a new signer, your SCA address — and all your funds — stay the same.
walletHowItWorks.sectionBackupBody: Your EOA key shards are automatically backed up via iCloud Keychain (iOS) or Google Password Manager (Android), protected by your login. You can also export the raw private key through Privy's secure recovery interface if you want full self-custody at any time.
walletHowItWorks.recoverIntro: Your funds are never locked in Kura. Follow these steps to access your Smart Account from any wallet app.
walletHowItWorks.step1After: , sign in with the same email you use in Kura, and download your EOA private key (64-character hex string). This is the signer key generated by Privy MPC.
walletHowItWorks.step2After: and choose "Import account → Private Key". Paste the key exported in Step 1. This gives you full control of the EOA signer.
walletHowItWorks.step3Before: Your actual funds live in the
walletHowItWorks.step3Mid: — the green address shown above, not the EOA. Open
walletHowItWorks.step3After: (or any Safe-compatible interface), add your SCA address on Base network, and connect the imported EOA as the owner. You now have full self-custody access.
walletHowItWorks.step4Body: Once connected in the Safe interface, you can send any token (USDC, ETH, etc.) directly to an external wallet or exchange address at any time — no Kura account required.
walletHowItWorks.warning: Never share your private key or recovery phrase. Kura will never ask for it.

legal.portfolioFooter: Kura is a self-custody wallet. Token swaps are routed by third-party services (Li.Fi). Kura is not a broker, exchange, or investment adviser.
legal.earnVault: Deposits and withdrawals execute on Base through your Kura Smart Wallet. Yield is provided by third-party Morpho vaults and curators. Kura is not a broker, exchange, or investment adviser. Rates vary; on-chain deposits involve smart contract risk.
legal.borrow: Borrowing, repayments, and collateral withdrawals execute on Base through your Kura Smart Wallet via Morpho Blue. Positions are subject to loan-to-value limits and may be liquidated if collateral value falls. Oracle prices and market rates are determined by third parties. Kura is not a broker, exchange, or investment adviser. On-chain borrowing involves smart contract and liquidation risk.
legal.swapTrade: Swaps are provided by third-party services (Li.Fi). Kura is not a broker or exchange and does not guarantee prices, routes, or execution.
legal.exchangeReadOnly: Kura only reads balances for portfolio tracking. Kura does not place orders or execute trades on your exchange account.
legal.securitiesTrade: Securities orders are submitted through Dinari, a third-party provider. Kura is not a broker-dealer or securities exchange.
legal.moonpay: Crypto purchases are processed by MoonPay, a third-party provider. Kura does not sell crypto or hold customer funds.
legal.bridge: Cross-chain transfers are routed by Li.Fi. Kura does not operate an exchange or hold bridged assets.
legal.cardWaitlist: Kura Card is not yet available. Joining the waitlist does not guarantee access. Kura is not a bank, money transmitter, or exchange.
legal.fiatRamp: Fiat deposits and withdrawals are processed by Bridge and other licensed partners. Kura is not a money transmitter.
legal.walletConnect: You interact with third-party dApps at your own risk. Kura does not control or endorse connected applications.
legal.riskSummary: Kura provides a self-custody wallet and portfolio tools. Kura is not a broker, exchange, investment adviser, or bank. Trading, swaps, card, and fiat services are provided by third parties. Digital assets involve risk of loss.
legal.tokenDeposit: Send only the selected token on Base to your Kura wallet address. Sending the wrong asset or network may result in permanent loss. Kura is not a bank, exchange, or investment adviser.
legal.trackfi: TrackFi is read-only portfolio tracking. Kura does not hold, custody, or control your funds and does not execute trades on your behalf. Connected bank, broker, and wallet APIs are used solely to read balances and holdings. Your financial data is protected with zero access encryption — only you can unlock it with your passkey. Kura is not a bank, broker, exchange, or investment adviser.
